$comment: SOURCE, NOT GENERATED. How a release reads on the changelog, shaped after Preline's (Zafar, 17 Sep 2026, pointing at preline.co/docs/changelog.html): a title, then chips (an icon and a label, like Preline's "New Components & Improvements" and "Fixes and Improvements"), each followed by its items with a bold lead ("People:", "Layout:") and the drawings the item is about. His asks on the way: "topic > icons, topic > icons. not all topics first and then all icons after that", "categorize them, not just text > icons. titles, etc.", "redrawns deserve to be a separate topic, not within a topic and each subtitle must carry shareable link like the main titles". So redraws are always their own chip. Per version: `title` (the release's headline, which every version has, released ones included, because the page heads each entry by it) and optionally `sections`: chips with `title`, `icon` (a drawing from this set, by name) or `logo` (a platform's own mark, for a chip about that platform, where a drawing of ours would stand in for someone else's trademark: `react`, drawn from components/brand-logos.tsx), `text`, and items in `sections` with `title`, `text`, `names` (added) or `redraws`. A version with no `sections` is drawn with default chips, New drawings and Redrawn, straight off git. pipeline/build-history.mjs gives every chip and item an `anchor` (v<version>-<chip>, v<version>-<chip>-<item>) that the site links, keeps only the drawings the entry carries, and appends anything no item claims in a last untitled group, reported, so a stale list never drops a drawing. Keyed by the version the work ships as, so nothing is re-keyed at the tag. Numbers go in as {names} and {files}. Anything in backticks is set as code, on the page and the Paper board both, the way a post sets an icon name. Where a version has sections they replace the note.

1.1.0.title: React Native support and 114 new drawings

sections.title: React Native
sections.text: The full set now works in React Native apps, Expo included, as `@keyline-icons/react-native`. Same names, styles and corners as the React package. Shared code between web and phone only changes the package name. On phone, color comes from a `color` prop: there's no text color to inherit.

1.0.0.title: 1,000 icons in stroke, two-tone, duotone and fill, each rounded and sharp: 8,000 total

sections.title: Four styles
sections.text: Every name now comes in four styles, stroke, two-tone, duotone and fill, and each style in two corner shapes, rounded and sharp: {files} SVGs across {names} names. The outlined duotone is called two-tone from this release, so an import of duotone that wants the old look changes to two-tone. Duotone is a new style with no outline, a grey body with the part that matters in black, drawn icon by icon.
